solutions.explanation:
Adding or subtracting the same expression on both sides preserves an inequality. We can therefore remove the terms that obscure the signs of the variables.

Adding \(y-x\) to both sides of \(x-y>x\) gives \(0>y\), so \(y<0\). Subtracting \(y\) from both sides of \(x+y<y\) gives \(x<0\).

Thus \(x\) and \(y\) are both strictly negative, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Isolate the sign information
